issues.description: Equality of FrameProcessor instances via `==` is not specified; use identity check.
issues.detail: In service_switcher.py the guard `frame.service == self.strategy.active_service` relies on `__eq__` for FrameProcessor. Since dataclasses or base objects may default to identity, this currently works, but the invariant being checked is identity ("the same processor instance"). Use `is` to state the invariant explicitly and avoid future breakage if FrameProcessor ever defines structural equality.

issues.description: Forward-reference type `"FrameProcessor"` on a dataclass field without TYPE_CHECKING import risks runtime resolution failures.
issues.detail: `ServiceSwitcherRequestMetadataFrame.service: "FrameProcessor"` uses a string annotation but frames.py likely has no `FrameProcessor` import. If any tooling calls `typing.get_type_hints()` on the dataclass it will raise NameError. Either import under `TYPE_CHECKING` or widen the annotation to `Any` and document the contract in the docstring.

issues.description: Invariant of the suppression rule is asymmetric and unstated for the inactive-service case.
issues.detail: The new guard suppresses the frame only when `frame.service == active_service`. The unstated invariant is: "a request targeting an inactive service should never reach `push_frame` because filters block it upstream." That assumption is load-bearing; if a future filter change lets such a frame through, it will leak downstream. State the invariant in a comment, or suppress all `ServiceSwitcherRequestMetadataFrame` regardless of target.

issues.description: Frame ordering change in STTService is correct but the postcondition deserves a literate comment.
issues.detail: The new order is `_push_stt_metadata()` then `push_frame(request)`. The old code suppressed the request; the new code forwards it. Downstream consumers now observe `[STTMetadataFrame, ServiceSwitcherRequestMetadataFrame]`. State this ordering as a one-line invariant comment so the next reader does not need to reverse-engineer why metadata precedes the request frame.

issues.description: No test exercises the inactive-service branch of the new conditional.
issues.detail: The change introduces a branch: suppress when target is active, otherwise let through. Tests verify the active path; the asymmetric branch (request targeting a non-active service arriving at `push_frame`) is unproven. Either add a test that establishes the upstream filter prevents this state, or add a test of the let-through behavior. Right now this is tried-correct, not proved-correct.

review.summary: UNDER-AUDITED. The rename and targeting refactor is clean and the existing tests still pass, but the new conditional in `ServiceSwitcher.push_frame` rests on two unstated invariants: that FrameProcessor equality means identity, and that requests targeting inactive services never reach this code path. Neither is documented or tested. The forward-reference type on the dataclass field also risks `get_type_hints()` failure. Mechanically correct; literately under-explained.
